  "c": "## Releases

A release is a pull request that changes the version, then a tag on its merge commit. [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) does the rest. Users refer to the action by its major tag, such as `cv/pi-action@v2`.

1. Make a branch from `main`, and set the version. `npm version` changes `package.json` and `package-lock.json`:

   ```bash
   git switch -c chore/release-X.Y.Z main
   npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version
   git commit -am "chore: release X.Y.Z"
   git push -u origin chore/release-X.Y.Z
   ```

2. Open a pull request with the title `chore: release X.Y.Z`. Write the notes in a `## Release notes` section of its description, in the [release notes format](#release-notes).
3. When CI passes, squash-merge the pull request.
4. Tag the merge commit on `main` with an annotated tag, and push the tag:

   ```bash
   git switch main && git pull
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m vX.Y.Z
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

5. `release.yml` makes sure that the tag agrees with `package.json` and is on `main`, and runs `npm run check`. Then it creates a draft GitHub Release with the `## Release notes` section, and moves the major tag (`vN`) to the commit. It does not move the major tag back for a tag that is earlier than the latest one.
6. Review the draft in [Releases](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases), and publish it.

### Release notes

Write the notes for users. Copy this structure:

```markdown
### Added
- **Short summary in bold** (#33, added in #44). What changed, for whom, and what to do, in a few sentences. See [Doc title](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/vX.Y.Z/docs/file.md#anchor).

### Fixed
- **Short summary in bold** (#42, fixed in #43). ...
```

- Use the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) headings, in this order: `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`, `Security`. Write only the headings that have items.
- Write one item for each change that users can see. Do not write items for CI, refactoring, or tests.
- After the summary, write the issue and the pull request, such as `(#42, fixed in #43)`. If there is no issue, write only the pull request, such as `(#43)`.
- Use full links to the docs of the tag (`blob/vX.Y.Z/...`), so that the links stay correct after later releases.
- Do not add the **Full Changelog** link. `release.yml` adds it.

## Pull requests",
  "pr": "{"body":"Closes #52.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **Overrides** (`03f2533`): if an extension has a tool with the same name as an earlier tool, the later tool replaces it, as with pi's `registerTool`. The log now says `pi-durable extension X replaces tool bash from coding-tools`. The new `src/thread.test.ts` tests wraps of tools and sections and the order they apply in (the last wrap wins). It also tests hiding a tool with `callers: [\"tools\"]` and replacing a tool.\n- **`exclude_tools` / `model_tools_hidden`** (`0cab9b8`): `exclude_tools` turns a tool off completely (`tools.remove`). `model_tools_hidden` keeps a tool away from the model, but other tools can still call it (`modelTools.remove`). Both accept `*` globs. Names are resolved after the extensions and their wraps are installed. A name that matches nothing gives a warning. If no tools are left for the model, the run fails. The inputs are applied on every run, so an empty input clears a setting from an earlier run. The `🤖` line now lists the tools the model gets.\n- **Prompt templates** (`94b273d`): a task that starts with `/<name>` is replaced by that template, with `$1`…, `$ARGUMENTS`/`$@`, `${@:N[:L]}` and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}` filled in one pass. Templates come from three places, in this order:\n  1. Each package's `pi.prompts`, including `pi.durable` packages.\n  2. `.pi/prompts`, only with `trust_project`.\n  3. `<agent_dir>/prompts`.\n\n  If two templates have the same name, the first one wins and the others get a warning. Expansion applies to the first message (also `{{task}}`), to follow-ups, and to `prompt` for `pr_number` and direct runs. Answers to questions are not expanded. The log shows what was typed: `▶ Request from @alice: /pit-reflect focus (prompt template from pit)`. The comment entry stores it in its `typed` and `template` fields.\n- **Docs**: `docs/extensions.md` (overrides, \"Tools the model sees\"), `docs/prompts.md` (prompt templates), `docs/security.md` (templates from the repository), `docs/how-it-works.md`, and the README input table.\n\n## Not in this PR\n\n- `model_tools_shown`: the docs say that the inputs only remove tools, so they can't bring back a tool that a wrap hid.\n- The optional section that lists the templates for the model (the issue says it should be off by default).\n- The pit change that hides the coding tools in `pit/durable` with wraps belongs in pit.\n\n`npm run check` passes.","closingIssuesReferences":[{"id":"I_kwDOQzT7dc8AAAABelN6bg","number":52,"repository":{"id":"R_kgDOQzT7dQ","name":"pi-action","owner":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU0NDU=","login":"cv"}},"url":"https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/52"}],"title":"feat: prompt templates, tool exclusion, and overrides from extensions"}
